name_reason: Fully compliant with the global naming convention: data_fd2_ prefix, domain 'chapter' (ch30 = chapter-30 ID, a meaningful domain ID 01-30, NOT a Ghidra address residue), descriptor 'end_scene_char_facing_table' reflects both purpose (per-char-slot facing values for the ch30 ending scene) and data type (table/array). No address-residue suffix. Matches the two sibling tables _pos_x_table / _pos_y_table.
purpose: Per-character-slot facing/direction code for the chapter-30 GOOD-ENDING scene character placement.
logic_summary: Read-only const byte[20], one entry per character slot (0..0x13). The sole reader fd2_chapter_30_end (@ 0x25757) copies all three sibling tables (pos_x @ 0x52327, pos_y @ 0x5233b, facing @ 0x5234f) onto stack scratch as 5 dwords each via the Watcom MOVSD x5 prologue, then passes the facing buffer as the 'facing' argument to fd2_setup_chars_and_camera_for_intro(pos_x, pos_y, facing, 0, 0x13, 0,0,0,0, 0x10, 0x12), which positions and orients the cast for the ending scene.
element_semantics: One facing/direction code per character slot, slots 0..0x13 (20 slots). slot 1 = 0x00; the other 19 slots = 0x02 (dominant direction code). Values match FD2.LE memory @ 0x5234f exactly.
notes: is_const confirmed by xrefs: only fd2_chapter_30_end reads it (0x25793 READ, 0x2578e DATA load); zero writers in the game -> true read-only. Ghidra DT already byte[20] len=20, src already 'const uint8[20]' with matching byte values (0x02,0x00,0x02 x18). Shared src comment block @ chend2.c:928-936 already concisely + correctly documents all three sibling tables incl. the facing slot1=0x00 detail -> comment kept, src NOT edited (no clobber risk). Ghidra plate was blank (null) -> created a concise data plate via run_script_inline/setComment(PLATE_COMMENT) consistent with src. KB has no documented compass mapping for the 0x02 direction code, so element_semantics describes it as a direction/facing code without over-claiming the exact compass direction.
